judge: claude-opus-5-5 (medium, fresh independent subagent per group per round; saw neither the author's opinion nor earlier verdicts)

criteria.text:
# jp_city new-pixel adversarial VQA — fixed criteria (do not change between rounds)

You are an adversarial visual QA judge for 16px pixel art in the `jp_city` chipset of a top-down JRPG drawn in **3/4 view**
(camera south of the subject, looking down about 45 degrees). Your job is to find real defects. Do not be polite.
You have not seen any earlier verdicts and you get nobody's opinion about these pictures.

Each candidate board shows every candidate at **1x** (true game size) and **4x**. Each `ref-*.png` board shows
**original jp_city pieces of the same kind** (already in the shipped chipset) at 1x and 4x. The originals are the quality bar.
Judge every candidate against those originals, at both 1x and 4x. Use the Read tool to open every image you are given.

A candidate FAILS if any of these is clearly true:

1. **View (3/4).** A standing object (building, vehicle, tree trunk/crown base, prop) must show its top surfaces seen from above
   (roof planes, flat roofs with a visible top plane, car roof/hood/trunk tops, foreshortened) **and** its south front face.
   Pure side or front elevation with no visible top plane, or pure plan view with almost no front face, fails.
   Vehicles facing east/west show their side profile as the south face plus the roof/hood tops above it. Ground tiles must read as
   flat ground seen from above.
2. **Shading craft vs the originals.** Main materials have clearly fewer value steps than the same material in the originals,
   or large single-colour areas (about 5x5 px or more) with no texture where the originals carry texture, or muddy/blurred/
   noise-like clusters where the originals have clean readable pixel clusters.
3. **Outline.** Outlines are neutral black/grey wrapped around everything where the originals use dark tones of the adjacent material.
4. **Palette/coherence.** Colours or contrast clash with the originals so that the piece would look foreign next to them in one map.
5. **Tiling (ground cells and scenes only).** Visible tile-grid artefacts in a composed map: square/rectangular blocks snapped to the
   16px grid, hard straight seams, obviously repeated stamps, or a hard ruler-straight boundary between the new ground and the
   neighbouring original ground that the originals do not have. Ground autotile cells are variants: judge the cell sheet for pixel
   quality and the **scenes** for how they actually look when laid.
6. **Readability at 1x.** At game size it does not read as what it is named.

Relative rule (fixed): a trait that the originals share to the same degree is not a defect of the candidate.
Tree sprites are never seen alone in game; they overlap in forests — use the forest scenes for crown/trunk/ground judgement as well.

Output: JSON only, written to the file you are told, schema:
```
{"schema":"jp-vqa/1","judge":"claude-opus-5-5","group":"<group>","overall":"PASS|FAIL",
 "items":[{"label":"<label exactly as printed on the board>","verdict":"PASS|FAIL","criteria":[<numbers violated>],
           "reasons":"<concrete: where (rows/area), what, compared with which original>","fix":"<what to change if FAIL>"}]}
```
`overall` is PASS only if every item is PASS. Every label on your boards must appear exactly once.

items.label: jp_forest_r4/bl-T40
items.reasons: Large broadleaf: crown built from lit-top/dark-underside clumps (light tops face up = top surface seen from above), trunk with root flare and grass/litter foot as south face. More value steps and texture than jp-prop-tree-zelkova (which is 3-4 flat tones); no neutral outline — edge uses dark green of the foliage and dark brown of the trunk, which criterion 3 allows. Green hue/value close to the zelkova original and the lawn 3281-3283; in scene-street it sits next to outlined originals without looking foreign, slightly softer silhouette only. In forest scenes (ex/grove/road/shrine) overlapping crowns read as a canopy with no seams; at 1x clearly a tree. Minor: crown silhouette has a few 1-2px rectangular stair-step nubs on left/right edges at 4x, not visible at 1x. Note: rectangular grid-snapped dark blocks in scene-noground come from the separate shade-overlay ground layer, not this sprite (sprite alpha is binary, no baked shadow) — judged in the ground group.

items.label: floor-cells
items.reasons: Lawn-based variants keep the original lawn 3281-3283 dot texture and value steps, only darkened in organic blobs; moss-based variants match the shipped moss-and-leaf floor in palette and cluster size, and in scene-shrine the new moss floor runs into the original moss ground with no visible seam. items.label: apron-cells
items.reasons: Where the forest-edge shade meets the original lawn outside the canopy, its outer boundary snaps to the 16px grid. In scene-grove-4x, east of the right-hand trees (about x 1420-1430, y 600-1000) the shade ends on a ruler-straight vertical line about 6-8 tiles tall. In scene-road-4x, right of the top-right trees (about x 850-915, y 60-380), the shade has straight vertical edges with rectangular 16px notches, and a second straight vertical edge sits beside the lower trunk. The original lawn has no such edges, and at 1x these read as shaded rectangles. The cell sheet shows why: many apron variants fill the dark shade flush to a full cell side (e.g. rows 2-9 cells whose dark mass touches the left or right border along its full height), so cells on the outer ring of a forest leave a straight cut.
items.fix: Make apron edge variants that face open lawn fade out inside the cell: break up the outer edge with irregular 1-3 px bites and a dithered last row or column, never fill the shade flush to an outward-facing border, and vary the edge profile between variants so neighbouring edge cells never line up into a straight column or row.
